description:
Convert Unix permissions between octal (755, 4755), symbolic (rwxr-xr-x) and ls -l strings, or apply a chmod expression such as 'go-w,u+x' to a starting mode. Explains each class, setuid/setgid/sticky bits and risky modes, and gives umask defaults.

Returns: JSON { octal, symbolic, ls, description[], warnings[], command, symbolicArg, umaskDefaults{ umask, newFile, newDirectory } }.
Example input: {"mode":"rwxr-x---"}
On error, includes hint: Use 1-4 octal digits, nine rwx characters (optionally with a leading file type), or a symbolic expression like u+x,go-w.

isDirectory.description: Treat the target as a directory (affects X and the ls -l type). Default false.

mode.description: Octal (644), symbolic or ls -l (-rwsr-xr-x), or a chmod expression (u+x, a=rX) applied to start.

start.description: Starting octal mode for expressions. Default 644 for files, 755 for directories.

umask.description: umask in octal, used for expressions without u/g/o/a and for new-file defaults. Default 022.

name: chmod_convert
title: chmod permission converter
